key_insight: The paper constructs hyperbolic color codes that achieve both constant encoding rate and polynomial code distance, overcoming the usual tradeoff seen in prior hyperbolic color-code designs.
engineering_relevance: This expands the design space for fault-tolerant quantum computing by offering high-rate qLDPC codes that preserve color-code structure useful for protocols like single-shot error correction.
method: Build on arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds that already support polynomial-distance hyperbolic toric codes.
Extend the construction to hyperbolic color codes in arbitrary dimension D ≥ 4.
Derive explicit polynomial lower-bound exponents for code distance and logical-qubit scaling by dimension and code type.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a constructive theoretical result with explicit scaling guarantees, including constant rate in even dimensions and polynomial scaling of both logical qubits and distance in other cases.
watch_item: The results are asymptotic and geometric, so practical code sizes, decoder performance, and hardware overhead may still be challenging to realize.
paper_title: Hyperbolic color codes with constant rate and polynomial distance
